step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture represents Zigbang's hybrid compute and database infrastructure on AWS. Incoming client traffic is resolved via external Route 53 and routed to CloudFront. CloudFront forwards traffic to an internal Route 53 DNS instance, which performs real-time weighted traffic splitting between an ECS on Fargate path and an API Gateway with Lambda path. A monitoring feedback loop reads ECS metrics via CloudWatch, triggering an AWS SDK logic component (represented via Lambda) to dynamically adjust internal Route 53 weights based on real-time traffic spikes and scaling needs. Both compute backends (Fargate and Lambda) interact with four database/storage systems: ElastiCache (caching), DocumentDB (unstructured/high-read data), RDS (relational CRUD), and OpenSearch/ElasticSearch (search and logging). CDK is used for infrastructure management.
